aspect: The name comes from a section of the criminal code
description: '419' is Section 419 of the Nigerian Criminal Code, which deals with obtaining by false pretences. By 1995 the association was strong enough that Nigeria amended its criminal code specifically to address the fraud, and the government has estimated that advance-fee scams damaged Nigeria's international reputation more than any other factor.
energy_note: A national reputation, named after a paragraph number.

aspect: The format is older than Nigeria's involvement in it
description: The structure predates the country entirely: the 18th-century 'Spanish Prisoner' con promised a reward to anyone paying for a trapped relative's release. Nigeria's name attached to it by an accident of timing - cheap fax and email arriving alongside an economic collapse.
energy_note: An eighteenth-century European con, filed under your country.

aspect: THE IRONY THAT MATTERS - the scammers do not present as Nigerian
description: In a study of 50 convicted romance scammers, 46% posed as white American males, 12% as military personnel and 10% as white European males. Posing as white is the standard tactic. So the men actually running the fraud are invisible as Nigerians, while ordinary Nigerians using their real names and faces absorb the entire suspicion.
energy_note: The scammer is pretending to be American. You are the one who looks Nigerian.
notes: This single row is the logical centre of the REP category.

aspect: The scale of the losses that fuel the reputation
description: FTC data put total US romance scam losses at $1.14 billion in 2023 with more than 64,000 victims. The harm is real, which is precisely why the collective attribution is so hard to argue against.
energy_note: The damage is real. The billing of it to 220 million people is not.

aspect: The socioeconomic engine, stated without excusing it
description: Among convicted offenders studied, 81.7% were under 26 and 74% were university students, against youth unemployment estimated at 53.4% for 15-to-34-year-olds and average monthly income comparable to 1980 levels.
energy_note: Mostly students, mostly under twenty-six, mostly with nothing else.

description: She says where she is from at a work social. There is a half-second pause, and then someone makes the prince joke, and everyone laughs including her, because the alternative is to be the person who could not take it. She has done this perhaps two hundred times.
energy_note: Laughing at it, again, because not laughing costs more.

description: Slower trust, more verification, fewer introductions, more scrutiny of the same work. None of it appears in a performance review and all of it accumulates across a career.
money_note: Lifetime earnings effect of a reputational headwind.
energy_note: A career run at a slightly worse exchange rate.
